label: Platformer or top-down game (Phaser)
description: A 2D platformer or top-down game on Phaser, bundled with its licence (MIT): jump, run, explore. Nothing to install, plays in any browser.
task: Make a browser game in this empty folder that needs nothing installed: index.html, style.css and src/main.js as ES modules, on Phaser 3. Dim Factory already put Phaser in lib/phaser/phaser.min.js (MIT, its licence in lib/LICENSES/phaser.txt): load it with a plain <script src="lib/phaser/phaser.min.js"> before your module and use the global Phaser; never load it from a CDN. Dim Factory also put starter modules in src/engine/ (MIT): loop.js (fixed 60 Hz step), rng.js (seeded randomness), input.js (keyboard, touch buttons, gamepad, remappable), storage.js (versioned local saves that never throw) and test-hook.js (window.__game, only with ?test=1); docs/game-test-hook.md explains the hook. Run the game rules on loop.js (update with its fixed dt; let Phaser draw), so stepping the hook is exact. Use Arcade Physics only. Draw all art in code (Phaser Graphics, generated textures, pixel art from text). Every game has: a title scene with how to play and a start button; play; pause with P or Esc and when the window loses focus; game over or a win with the score and Restart; a Settings scene for keys, sound, reduced motion and a colour-safe palette, saved with storage.js. Big on-screen buttons drive the same actions on a phone. Sound, if any, is made with the Web Audio API after the first key or tap. Use original names, characters and art: familiar mechanics are fine, but never copy a famous game's name, characters, logo, art, music or sounds. Everything the game uses is in the project: no CDN, no network, no third-party scripts, ads or trackers, no eval or new Function. Text a player types is shown with textContent. In src/main.js wire the test hook with a state() that reports scene ('title', 'playing', 'paused', 'over' or 'won'), score, lives and level, and a setSeed that restarts with a seed. Write the plan's acceptance criteria as things a player does and sees, and write playtest.json (data, not code) with one scenario per criterion, as docs/game-test-hook.md shows: Dim Factory plays it with real key presses as a Verify check, so a scenario marked must has to pass. Keep the rules (levels as data, scoring) in plain modules under src/game/ with no DOM or Phaser in them, and add a package.json with one script, test, that runs node --test on tests/*.test.mjs. Add a README.md: how to play, how to open it (Play it in Dim Factory, or serve the folder with any static server), how to run the tests, how to share it (zip it and upload to itch.io as an HTML5 game), and credits (Phaser, MIT; the starter files from Dim Factory, MIT). Make it feel good to play: every action gets clear feedback (a sound, a flash or a small movement), the first moments are easy and it gets harder step by step, and the end of a game shows how it went with a quick way to play again.
